text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

The panel's composition doesn't help you. You're a man, the successful candidate is a man, and the panel was all men — there's no pattern suggesting your sex counted against you. Raising it would read as grasping, and would weaken the parts of your case that are genuinely strong.

Those parts are real: a completed PhD versus an unfinished one, six papers versus two, four years of teaching for a teaching post. If "industry experience" wasn't weighted in the advertised criteria, that's a scoring problem worth challenging.

Focus instead on the unanswered request. Most public universities have a deadline for written reasons. Chase it formally, in writing, citing their own procedure, and escalate to the HR director if needed.
